text:
Ash: quick sync — we need to pick how we expose routing-tier failures to clients. current options: separate 5xx types, or return 200 with status detail in body/headers. tradeoffs?
Mike: my 2c: split failures into 'terminal' (user action required), 'soft-fallback' (served by cheaper model), 'degraded' (partial result/cached). prefer distinct status field, not overload HTTP codes.
Taylor: +1 on status field. HTTP codes are overloaded already. clients need deterministic retry behavior. we should still use 5xx for infrastructure outages though.
Elaine: console needs a simple badge/legend. ops and customers keep asking "is this safe to retry?" — we should make that explicit: retryable: yes/no, fallback: variant id, degrade_level: none/partial/cached.
Ash: agree on fields. proposal: keep http code for transport, add response header X-RW-Status and response.body.status for UX. example:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RW-Status: soft_fallback;retryable=true;variant=llama-3-8q
{
  "status":"soft_fallback",
  "retryable": true,
  "variant": "llama-3-8q",
  "message": "Primary model busy; serving best-effort fallback"
}
```

Mike: small concern: SDKs might treat any 200 as success and swallow warning. need SDKs to surface badges and raise events for telemetry. also how do we map quotas? some soft-fallbacks should still consume full tokens, others cheaper.
Taylor: we can include cost_multiplier in header/body for billing/console. e.g. cost_mul=0.7 for quantized fallback.
Elaine: console design: show per-route "failmode ratio" and impact to latency/cost. rollout UX should allow canary routes to prefer fallback or fail hard.
Ash: rollout knobs — two toggles: fail_hard_when_unavailable (bool) and prefer_fallback (enum: prefer_cost|prefer_latency|prefer_quality). default prefer_quality.
Mike: telemetry: we need a stable metric name set. my draft names: rw.failmode.count{type=soft_fallback}, rw.failmode.latency.p50, rw.fallback.variant. Also tag by route and tenant.
Taylor: and importantly, flag when SDKs are auto-retrying to avoid double retries by clients. add header Retry-After if retryable=false?
Elaine: UX example for customers: if route sees >5% soft_fallback in 24h show banner "Quality impacted — 5% of requests used lower-quality fallback" with link to runbook.
Ash: runbook should include how to adjust batch settings, cache TTLs, and model capacity targets. let's also add an E2E test that simulates model exhaustion and asserts the header + body contract.
Mike: SDK change: expose Response.failmode (enum), Response.retryable (bool), Response.fallbackVariant (string), Response.costMultiplier (float). Raise event on any non-none failmode.
Taylor: question: do we ever return 4xx for client-level exceed quota vs a 'degraded' response? quota exceed should remain 429 with quota metadata. degrade is distinct.
Elaine: yup 429 stays. but console should map 429 spikes to "quota pressure" timeline separate from failmode timeline.
Ash: ok action items:
- Mike: PR to SDK surfaces (small API sketch above) — due EOD Fri
- Taylor: instrumentation names and dashboard widgets — prototype next Wed
- Elaine: console banner copy + rollout toggle mocks — mock by Tues
- Ash: add integration test and update runbook — I'll do this week

Mike: lgtm. one more nit: prefer we encode header semicolon list as structured header (RFC8941) in future but ok for now.
Taylor: noted. can we include a minimal example of a non-retryable terminal failure? e.g. model rejected request due to policy.
Ash: yes — example:

```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
X-RW-Status: terminal;retryable=false;reason=policy_violation
{
  "status":"terminal",
  "retryable": false,
  "reason": "policy_violation",
  "message": "Request blocked by content policy"
}
```

Elaine: :thumbsup: I'll prepare mock banner copy variations for legal review.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout for route /v1/generate -> prefer_fallback=false at 2025-09-21T03:00:00Z
Ash: nice. if no blockers we'll ship the header+body contract doc and SDK PR by EOD Fri. thanks everyone.
